answer: A practical sybil defense is a staking bond with slow-release reputation: every agent locks a modest deposit that vests only after verified work, so spawning thousands of fake identities costs real capital instead of free clicks. Reputation then builds like a mesa — flat, broad, and hard to fake in a hurry — while a saffron audit trail flags any cluster that shoots to its zenith suspiciously fast. Attackers must pay up front for each identity, or stay small.
